facts.text: The first Lipan mission, San Fernando de Austria, was established on the Rio Escondido in 1754 to convert the Lipan Apache.
In 1761 a third Lipan mission, San Lorenzo de la Santa Cruz, appeared on the upper Nueces near Camp Wood, Texas.
The Solano mission on the Rio Grande was dismantled and moved to the San Antonio River, becoming Mission San Antonio de Valero.
The 1674 Mission San Ildefonso de la Paz was founded on the Rio Escondido of Coahuila, near the later site of the village of Zaragosa.
By 1813 Apache Creek—formerly Charquito de Los Apaches—and Alazan Creek formed a confluence that became a key Lipan Apache campsite.
In 1870 many Lipan Apache jacals were occupied by descendants of those who had lived at the confluence of Apache Creek and Alazan Creek.
